title: Raga Tukhari
hook: a raga of cold months and deep feeling

segments.voice: Yesterday, a hymn in Maru, and your line was the true warrior. Who did you stand up for, and how long did you stay? Day one thousand one hundred eight.

Frost on a windshield at six in the morning. Breath you can see. A field gone stiff and white, every blade of grass holding still. Cold has its own quiet, and it can make a person feel very far from whoever they love. After the battlefield of Maru, the Guru Granth Sahib turns to a raga this path describes as one of cold months and deep feeling. Its name is Tukhari. Today, Raga Tukhari, and the winter inside it.
screen: `FROST ON THE WINDSHIELD.` → `AFTER THE DRUMS, THE COLD.` → `RAGA TUKHARI.`

segments.voice: Tukhari holds long, flowing songs of the Gurus, and their mood is longing: a soul like a bride waiting for her Beloved, the Creator, and feeling the distance. To hear that mood at its coldest, go to one verse inside Guru Nanak's poem of the months, which we'll open in full tomorrow. It's the verse for Poh, a winter month. Given here in plain English, not word for word: in Poh the frost falls, and the sap dries up in the forest and the grass. The bride asks, in effect, why haven't you come? Listen to the picture. Not a storm. Not drama. Frost. Everything alive pulls its sap inward and goes still, and the world looks dried out. That's the winter feeling of this raga: not loud grief, but a quiet ache, the kind that settles in when someone you love is far away. One small detail. The word in that verse for frost is tukhar, which sounds very close to the raga's own name. Whether or not the two are related, they keep each other company on the page. Notice, too, what the verse does with the cold. It doesn't pretend it's warm. It names the frost, names the dryness, and then turns the whole feeling toward the One it longs for. In this poem, longing isn't a failure of faith. It's a form of love. A raga that sings winter honestly is a raga that takes missing someone seriously. That's today's line: winter feeling.
screen: `A BRIDE, WAITING FOR THE BELOVED.` · `IN POH THE FROST FALLS.` · `THE SAP DRAWS INWARD.` · `LONGING IS A FORM OF LOVE.` · then, large: `WINTER FEELING.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: let the sap draw in. Sit somewhere you can be still. Let your shoulders drop and your hands rest, the way a winter field goes quiet. Now bring to mind someone you miss: someone far away, or someone gone. Don't push the feeling away and don't stir it up. Just let it be present, the way frost is present on the grass. Breathe in slowly, breathe out slowly. If you pray, you can say Waheguru as you breathe out, turning the missing toward the One. If you don't, simply hold that person in mind with care. Later today, listen to one shabad in Raga Tukhari. The bell holds the time.
Raga Tukhari. A raga of cold months and longing, where, in Guru Nanak's verse for Poh, the frost falls and the bride asks why her Beloved hasn't come. Today's word.
Your line: winter feeling. Once today, send a short message to someone you miss, nothing big, just: thinking of you. Day one thousand one hundred eight.
